recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Identity That Has To Die", "body": "Elise Frosch, who runs Family Fungi with her husband James, describes motherhood as an initiation rather than a job description. She was 24 when Joffrey was born, had never babysat, and spent those years pulled between festivals, dancing and hooping, and an identity she had not yet put down. Only after her second son, Manu, did she feel she had submitted to the archetype of the great mother. The struggle she sees in other women, she argues, comes from trying to be maiden and mother at once instead of letting the older self be reborn."}, {"title": "Alchemy Mapped Onto Birth", "body": "Chance Garton walks through calcination, dissolution and separation while Elise maps each onto pregnancy and labour. She reads the ring of fire, the crowning moment hospital obstetrics files as transition between nine and ten centimetres, as the burning away of doubt. Chance notes calcination also fits early breastfeeding, where blood is transmuted into a white material. Elise tells how brutal first trimester nausea stopped the day she noticed her makeshift trash can was a water filter box printed with the words purified the natural way, and read the sickness as purification instead."}, {"title": "Breast Milk, Formula And The Argument Over Both", "body": "This is the sharpest stretch of the stream. Elise reads commercial formula as soybean oil, whey isolate and fortified vitamins, and points women instead toward the Weston A. Price homemade recipe or donor milk, noting she sourced another mother's milk for a week when antibiotics interrupted nursing Manu. Chance claims that in his biofield tuning work, people fed formula commonly show a lack mentality and approval seeking he traces to the sacral chakra, offered as his own observation rather than evidence. Slick Dissident goes further, calling the formula economy a deliberate severing of the family bond."}, {"title": "Name Magic And The Weave", "body": "Slick Dissident named his daughter Lyra months before her birth, then learned the sun passes through the Lyra constellation on her birthday and that the Lyrids open his calendar of twenty major meteor showers. Her middle names, Bell and Everly, turned out to hide the word rebel. Elise assembled Ja Free Will out of reggae, a friend's offhand suggestion, and a name her eldest now lives out at full volume. Chance reads a passage arguing Emmanuel begins in Hebrew with om rather than I, with the word for virgin buried inside it."}, {"title": "Martyr Means Witness", "body": "Slick Dissident closes with a weave on the December drone panic, claiming the silhouettes match the Hercules constellation and that martyrdom always needs an audience, since the Greek word for martyr means witness and nobody can be a martyr in private. Chance pushes back on the etymology, noting the Latin looking ending on the spelling he found. Elise then turns the same word inward: no midwife, ceremony or bystander can confirm your passage into motherhood, so the mother has to witness the maiden herself. Chance also recommends Nathaniel Branden's Six Pillars of Self-Esteem."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Elise Frosch is the magna mater of Family Fungi, where she and husband James create the culture they want to spread in the world by providing mushrooms and magical mycelial medicines, along with home grown herbal products and spagyric tinctures. Today we'll talk about Elise's insights into the alchemical nature of a woman's identity transformation through the right of passage from maidenhood to motherhood.
